title: China win both U19 team titles at the World Youth Championships, beating Taiwan and Japan 3-1
seo_title: World Youth Championships 2026: China win U19 team titles
description: China beat Taiwan and Japan 3-1 to win both U19 team titles at the World Youth Championships in Istanbul, with Wen Ruibo and Jiang Yiyi winning twice.
standfirst: Wen Ruibo and Jiang Yiyi won both their singles in the finals in Istanbul, and Taiwan's boys took silver, their best result since the championships moved to under-19 teams in 2021.
body: China won both under-19 team titles at the ITTF World Youth Championships in Istanbul on Monday, beating Taiwan 3-1 in the boys' final and Japan 3-1 in the girls'.

Both finals started at 3pm UK time and both took more than two hours: the boys' final lasted 2hr 16min and the girls' 2hr 10min. In each, China's leading player won twice. Wen Ruibo, the world No 14, did not drop a game in his first match and came through a deciding game in his second, and 16-year-old Jiang Yiyi won the opening and closing matches of the girls' final.
## Taiwan strike first in the boys' final

Taiwan took the lead. Hung Che-Yen, 17 and ranked 128th in the world, beat Li Hechen 11-9, 6-11, 11-6, 11-7 in the first match. In July Hung won the men's singles at WTT Feeder Ulaanbaatar without dropping a game in the semi-final or final.

Wen then levelled the tie, beating Lin Chin-Ting 11-5, 11-6, 11-9 in 22 minutes. Lin, 17, won a mixed doubles bronze at the [Youth Olympic Games in Dakar](/news/youth-olympic-games-dakar-2026-kawakami-matsushima-mixed-doubles-gold.html) this month. Yu Haiyang, 16, put China ahead by beating Yang Hao-Jen 11-7, 11-13, 11-7, 11-8. Yang, 19, earned his first place in Taiwan's senior national team at the [ranking trials](/news/yang-hao-jen-hung-jing-kai-taiwan-national-team-trials-2026.html) last week.

The fourth match, between the two players who had already won, went the distance. Wen won the first two games 11-8, 11-6, Hung took the next two 11-7, 11-9, and Wen then won the decider 11-2 to take the title for China.

Taiwan's silver is their best result in the boys' team event since the championships changed in 2021 from a single under-18 category to under-19 and under-15 events. Their boys won bronze in 2022 and 2025, and before the change had won two silver and three bronze medals. Taiwan reached the final by beating India 3-0, after China had come from 2-1 down to beat Japan 3-2 in the [semi-finals](/news/world-youth-championships-2026-u19-team-semi-finals-wen-ruibo-jiang-yiyi-china-taiwan.html). Taiwan's girls went out in the quarter-finals.
## Jiang wins twice against Japan

Jiang, who turned 16 last week, opened the girls' final with a five-game win over Yuna Ojio, the world No 88, taking the decider 11-4 after a match of 44 minutes. Mao Takamori levelled for Japan by beating Yao Ruixuan 12-10, 11-8, 11-3.
Li Yihui, 17, then beat Misuzu Takeya, Japan's highest-ranked player at 71st in the world, 11-6, 11-7, 11-8. Jiang finished the final by beating Takamori 11-5, 11-9, 12-10 in 26 minutes.

Jiang won both her singles in the semi-final against France without dropping a game, so she won four matches out of four across the last two rounds. Japan had beaten the United States 3-0 in the other semi-final.
## Mixed doubles: Chinese pairs into the last eight

Earlier on Monday the under-19 mixed doubles reached the quarter-finals. Wen and Jiang beat Romania's Robert Istrate and Bianca Mei-Rosu 11-6, 13-11, 11-8, and Li Hechen and Yao came through a deciding game against India's Priyanuj Bhattacharyya and Syndrela Das, 10-12, 11-6, 3-11, 11-5, 11-6.

Japan have two pairs in the last eight. Shunto Iwaida and Takamori beat Samuel Arpas and Maria Berzosa 11-3, 11-4, 11-0, and Kohaku Nakano and Aoba Takahashi came from a game down to beat Francesco Trevisan and Eseniia Shirokova 3-1. Patryk Zyworonek of Poland and Germany's Koharu Itagaki, France's Antoine Noirault and Leana Hochart, South Korea's Lee Hyeonho and Heo Yerim and India's Abhinandh Pradhivadhi and Divyanshi Bhowmick are also through.
## What's next
The quarter-finals are on Tuesday at 12.30pm UK time:

- Wen Ruibo and Jiang Yiyi (CHN) v Patryk Zyworonek and Koharu Itagaki (POL/GER)
- Li Hechen and Yao Ruixuan (CHN) v Lee Hyeonho and Heo Yerim (KOR)
- Shunto Iwaida and Mao Takamori (JPN) v Antoine Noirault and Leana Hochart (FRA)
- Abhinandh Pradhivadhi and Divyanshi Bhowmick (IND) v Kohaku Nakano and Aoba Takahashi (JPN)

The semi-finals follow later in the day, along with the last 16 and quarter-finals of the boys' and girls' doubles. Times are approximate. Results, the draw and live scores are on [Eleven's event page](/events/world-youth-championships-2026.html#matches).
## Results in full

- U19 boys' team final: China bt Taiwan 3-1. Hung Che-Yen (TPE) bt Li Hechen (CHN) 11-9, 6-11, 11-6, 11-7; Wen Ruibo (CHN) bt Lin Chin-Ting (TPE) 11-5, 11-6, 11-9; Yu Haiyang (CHN) bt Yang Hao-Jen (TPE) 11-7, 11-13, 11-7, 11-8; Wen Ruibo bt Hung Che-Yen 11-8, 11-6, 7-11, 9-11, 11-2
- U19 girls' team final: China bt Japan 3-1. Jiang Yiyi (CHN) bt Yuna Ojio (JPN) 11-8, 11-13, 11-6, 8-11, 11-4; Mao Takamori (JPN) bt Yao Ruixuan (CHN) 12-10, 11-8, 11-3; Li Yihui (CHN) bt Misuzu Takeya (JPN) 11-6, 11-7, 11-8; Jiang Yiyi bt Mao Takamori 11-5, 11-9, 12-10
